links.comparator_used: Static reweighing and a no-intervention baseline across 15 simulated retraining cycles on MIMIC-IV (30 runs, 16 intersectional subgroups)
links.outcome: TPR gap across retraining cycles (final gap, trajectory stability), and post-shift TPR-gap spike under covariate shift
links.effect: Final TPR gaps did not differ among the three strategies (Friedman chi2(2)=1.195, p=0.550). The adaptive controller showed bounded, damped trajectories where static reweighing showed larger transient spikes. Under covariate shift, the post-shift TPR-gap spike was +0.091 with adaptive control vs +0.139 with no intervention.
links.quote: Across 30 independent runs, all three strategies converge to final TPR gaps with no significant difference (Friedman $\chi ^{2}(2)=1.195$, $p=0.550$); however, the Dynamic Adaptive Fairness controller exhibits bounded, damped trajectories where static reweighing shows larger transient spikes.

design_hint: dynamic fairness monitoring and adaptive retraining control under drift
